{{Short description|Curve which could be used to trisect an angle with compass and straightedge}}
{{CS1 config|mode=cs2}}
In [[geometry]], a '''trisectrix''' is a curve which can be used to [[angle trisection|trisect an arbitrary angle]] with ruler and compass and this curve as an additional tool. Such a method falls outside those allowed by [[compass and straightedge constructions]], so they do not contradict the well known theorem which states that an arbitrary angle cannot be trisected with that type of construction. There is a variety of such curves and the methods used to construct an angle trisector differ according to the curve. Examples include:
* [[Limaçon trisectrix]] (some sources refer to this curve as simply the trisectrix.)<ref>{{EB1911|noprescript=1|wstitle=Trisectrix |volume=27}}</ref><ref name=yates>{{citation|title=The trisection problem, chapter II: Solutions by means of curves|first=Robert C.|last=Yates|journal=National Mathematics Magazine|volume=15|issue=4|date=January 1941|pages=191–202|doi=10.2307/3028133 |jstor=3028133}}</ref>
* [[Trisectrix of Maclaurin]]<ref>{{citation
 | last = Dudley | first = Underwood | author-link = Underwood Dudley
 | isbn = 0883855143
 | page = 12
 | publisher = Cambridge University Press
 | title = The Trisectors
 | year = 1994}}; {{Google books|tp3kHvbMjqUC|excerpt|page=12}}</ref>
* [[Tschirnhausen cubic]] (a.k.a. Catalan's trisectrix and L'Hôpital's cubic)<ref>{{citation
 | last = Farouki | first = Rida T.
 | doi = 10.1007/978-3-540-73398-0
 | isbn = 978-3-540-73397-3
 | mr = 2365013
 | pages = 398–399
 | publisher = Springer
 | series = Geometry and Computing
 | title = Pythagorean-Hodograph Curves: Algebra and Geometry Inseparable
 | volume = 1
 | year = 2008}}</ref>
* [[Deslanges trisectrix]]<ref>{{citation
 | last = Mortini | first = Raymond
 | doi = 10.1007/s00283-023-10277-3
 | issue = 2
 | journal = The Mathematical Intelligencer
 | mr = 4754352
 | pages = 135–140
 | title = Turning conics into beans: introducing the haricoids
 | volume = 46
 | year = 2024}}</ref>
* [[Cubic parabola]] (the graph of the cube function)<ref name=yates/>
* [[Hyperbola]] with eccentricity 2<ref>{{citation|title=An Algebraic System of Conic Sections, and Other Curves|first=J. M. F.|last=Wright|location=London|publisher=Black and Armstrong|year=1836|contribution=257. To trisect any angle by the hyperbola|page=206|contribution-url=https://archive.org/details/analgebraicsyst00wriggoog/page/n242}}</ref><ref name=yates/>
* [[Parabola#As_trisectrix|Parabola]]<ref name=yates/>
* [[Cycloid of Ceva]]<ref name=yates/>

A related concept is a '''sectrix''', which is a curve which can be used to divide an arbitrary angle by any integer.<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.mathcurve.com/courbes2d.gb/sectrice/sectrice.shtml|title=Sectrix curve|first=Robert|last=Ferréol|year=2017|work=Encyclopédie des formes mathématiques remarquables|access-date=2025-10-20}}</ref> Examples include:
* [[Archimedean spiral]]<ref>{{cite book |first1=Uta B.|last1=Merzbach|author1-link=Uta Merzbach| first2=Carl B. | last2=Boyer | author2-link=Carl Benjamin Boyer | title=A History of Mathematics | pages = 113–114 | edition=Third | publisher=John Wiley & Sons | year=2011|isbn=978-0470525487}}</ref>
* [[Quadratrix of Hippias]]<ref>{{citation|title=An investigation of historical geometric constructions|journal=Convergence|url=https://old.maa.org/press/periodicals/convergence/an-investigation-of-historical-geometric-constructions|date=July 2006|first1=Suzanne|last1=Harper|first2=Shannon|last2=Driskell|publisher=Mathematical Association of America}}</ref><ref name=yates/>
* [[Sine curve]]<ref>{{citation
 | last = Sheng | first = Hung Tao
 | doi = 10.1080/0025570X.1969.11975925
 | journal = [[Mathematics Magazine]]
 | jstor = 2689193
 | mr = 240707
 | pages = 73–80
 | title = A method of trisection of an angle and {{mvar|X}}-section of an angle
 | volume = 42
 | year = 1969
 | issue = 2
 }}</ref>

==See also==
*[[Sectrix of Maclaurin]], a family of curves different members of which can divide angles into different numbers of parts
*[[Neusis construction]], the use of a marked ruler in constructions such as angle trisection
*[[Quadratrix]], a curve used for [[squaring the circle]]
